deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page is not Riemann's own research text. It is a draft of the editorial commentary (Weber, drawing on Dedekind, as the previous page says) on Riemann's 1861 Paris prize essay, the Commentatio mathematica. That commentary was printed in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876). The page derives the basic properties of Riemann normal coordinates.

Setup (previous page): the metric is ds^2 = sum a_{ii'} dx_i dx_{i'}, where x_i = r c_i and r is geodesic distance from the point 0. Along each geodesic from 0 the c_i are constant. The geodesic equations d(sum_i a_{mu i} c_i)/dr = 1/2 sum (d a_{ii'}/dx_mu) c_i c_{i'}, multiplied by r^2, give
(2) sum_{ii'} p_{mu i i'} x_i x_{i'} = 0, with p_{mu i i'} = d_{i'} a_{i mu} + d_i a_{i' mu} - d_mu a_{ii'} (twice the Christoffel symbol of the first kind).
Equivalently:
(2*) sum d_mu a_{ii'} x_i x_{i'} = 2 sum d_{i'} a_{mu i} x_i x_{i'}.

The top third of this page (crossed out, with diagonal strokes) is an abandoned first attempt. The surviving text redoes it as follows.

(a) Put omega_mu = sum_i a_{mu i} x_i. Then d omega_mu/dx_nu = a_{mu nu} + sum_i (d a_{mu i}/dx_nu) x_i.
[Mine: from this, sum d_mu a_{ii'} x x = sum_i (d_mu omega_i) x_i - omega_mu and sum d_{i'} a_{mu i} x x = sum_i (d_i omega_mu) x_i - omega_mu.] So (2*) becomes
omega_mu + sum_i (d omega_i/dx_mu) x_i = 2 sum_i (d omega_mu/dx_i) x_i.

(b) Put 2 omega = sum omega_i x_i. Then 2 d omega/dx_mu = omega_mu + sum_i d_mu omega_i x_i. Hence d omega/dx_mu = D omega_mu, where D = sum x_i d/dx_i is the Euler operator.
Differentiating: d^2 omega/dx_mu dx_nu = d_nu omega_mu + D(d_nu omega_mu).
Symmetry of second derivatives then gives F + DF = 0 for F = d_nu omega_mu - d_mu omega_nu. By Euler's theorem F is homogeneous of degree -1: f(t x) = t^{-1} f(x).

(c) If the a_{ii'} and their derivatives are finite at 0, then f(x) = t f(tx) tends to 0 as t tends to 0. So f = 0, i.e. d_nu omega_mu = d_mu omega_nu.
Using a_{mu nu} = a_{nu mu}, this gives sum_i d_nu a_{mu i} x_i = sum_i d_mu a_{nu i} x_i.
[Mine: contract with x_nu.] Then sum d_{i'} a_{mu i} x_i x_{i'} = sum d_mu a_{ii'} x_i x_{i'}. Combined with (2*), both sums vanish: sum d_mu a_{ii'} x x - sum d_{i'} a_{mu i} x x = 0.
The marginal 'unde' formula is the generalized Gauss lemma. Since D omega_mu = omega_mu, omega_mu is homogeneous of degree 1. Hence sum_i a_{mu i}(rc) c_i = sum_i a^0_{mu i} c_i.

(d) General lemma: if alpha_{ii'} = alpha_{i'i} is smooth and sum alpha_{ii'} x_i x_{i'} = 0 identically, then at 0, differentiating twice and three times:
- alpha_{ii'}(0) = 0;
- the cyclic sum d_{i''} alpha_{ii'} + d_i alpha_{i'i''} + d_{i'} alpha_{i''i} = 0 at 0.

(e) Apply the lemma with alpha_{ii'} = p_{mu ii'} (symmetric in i, i'). This gives (3): p_{ii'i''} = 0 at 0, and the cyclic sum of first derivatives of p_{i...} vanishes at 0.

(f) Adding p_{ii'i''} = 0 and p_{i'ii''} = 0 gives 2 d_{i''} a_{ii'} = 0. This is (4): all first derivatives of the metric vanish at 0, i.e. Christoffel symbols vanish at the origin of normal coordinates.

The second relation in (3) is used on the next page. There it yields the symmetries of the second derivatives, and from them the 1/3-curvature term of the metric expansion in normal coordinates.
errors: 'posito t=0' is loose. Homogeneity f(tx) = t^{-1} f(x) holds for t > 0 only; the correct argument is the limit f(x) = lim_{t->0+} t f(tx) = 0, using finiteness of f at 0. The conclusion is correct.
The crossed-out opening section contains slips: inconsistent notation Theta, an unfinished sentence 'ordinis [?]', and the garbled 'ebenso'. The author abandoned it and rewrote it below.
The marginal note read as 'ist hier fehlerhaft' does not point to an actual error. The argument as rewritten is valid.
Minor: before (4), the image reads 'addendo p_{i' i i''} = 0' (indices permuted). The transcription's 'p_{i i' i''}' would give nothing new.

results.what: In geodesic polar/normal coordinates x = r c, the geodesic equations reduce to sum_{ii'} p_{mu ii'} x_i x_{i'} = 0 (Christoffel combination contracted with x twice).
results.modern_name: Characterization of Riemann normal coordinates (Gamma^k_{ij}(x) x^i x^j = 0)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1854 Habilitation, 1861 Commentatio); explicit derivation in Weber/Dedekind's commentary in Riemann's Werke (1876)

results.what: Euler-operator/homogeneity argument showing d_nu omega_mu = d_mu omega_nu, hence sum_i a_{mu i}(x) x_i = sum_i a^0_{mu i} x_i.
results.modern_name: Generalized Gauss lemma in normal coordinates
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (1827) for surfaces; n-dim form in Riemann's Werke commentary (Dedekind/Weber 1876)

results.what: A symmetric alpha with sum alpha x x = 0 identically has alpha(0) = 0 and vanishing cyclic sum of first derivatives at 0. Applied to p, this gives d a_{ii'}/dx_{i''} = 0 at 0.
results.modern_name: Vanishing of first derivatives of the metric / Christoffel symbols at the origin of normal coordinates

deep.surprise_reason: This is the draft of the editors' (Weber/Dedekind) commentary on the Commentatio mathematica, printed in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876). The content (normal coordinates, Gauss lemma, vanishing first derivatives) is standard and already published.
